[E_MUL_REAL_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Mul** multiplies tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the product of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i] $$ where - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$. The multiplication is exact: $C[i]$ is the product in $\mathbb{R}$ of the two elements, with no approximation, and it is defined for every pair of real numbers. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the product of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]
- `[E_MUL_REAL_CONSTR_A_0010]` Shape compatibility - Statement: The shapes of $A$ and $B$ are compatible for broadcasting.
- `[E_MUL_REAL_CONSTR_B_0010]` Shape compatibility - Statement: see constraint [E_MUL_REAL_CONSTR_A_0010](#E_MUL_REAL_CONSTR_A_0010) on tensor $A$.

- `[E_MUL_REAL_CONSTR_C_0010]` Shape definition
  - Statement: Tensor $C$ has the shape of $A$ and $B$ broadcast to a common shape.

[E_MUL_FLOAT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Mul** multiplies tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise according to IEEE 754 floating-point semantics and stores the result in tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the floating-point product of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \tilde{A}[i] *_{(\text{f})} \tilde{B}[i] = \begin{cases} \text{NaN} & \text{if } \tilde{A}[i] \text{ or } \tilde{B}[i] \text{ is NaN, or if one of them is a zero and the other an infinity} \\ \sigma \cdot \infty & \text{if neither is NaN, one of them is an infinity, and the other is neither a zero nor NaN} \\ \text{round}(\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} $$ where - $*_{(\text{f})}$ is the multiplication of the floating-point type of $A$, $B$ and $C$, i.e. $*_{(\text{f16})}$, $*_{(\text{f32})}$ or $*_{(\text{f64})}$ according to that type, whereas the $*$ of the third case is the multiplication of $\mathbb{R}$: there, $\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact product of the two elements, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $\sigma \in \{-1, +1\}$ is the sign given by the rule of signs: $\sigma = -1$ when the operands have opposite signs and $\sigma = +1$ otherwise, the sign of an infinity and the sign of a zero being signs like any other, - $\text{round}(x)$ is the value of $x$ rounded to the nearest value of the type of $A$ and $B$ using the roundTiesToEven attribute of IEEE 754, the exponent range of the type being unbounded: a magnitude whose nearest value exceeds the largest finite value of the type of $A$ and $B$ gives an infinity of the sign of $x$. In the first case, an operand that is NaN is propagated, and the multiplication of a zero and an infinity is the invalid operation defined in IEEE 754 section 7.2; the result is NaN in both cases. The NaN of this case is a quiet NaN; its sign and its payload are not specified, whether the NaN comes from an operand or from the invalid operation, so that every quiet NaN of the type of $A$ and $B$ is a conforming result. In the second case, the product of an infinity and a nonzero finite value, or of two infinities, is an infinity whose sign is given by the rule of signs; the result involves no rounding. In the last case, both operands are finite, and the exact product is rounded as defined above. That product may be representable, in which case the result is that product and the multiplication is exact; it may be subnormal; and its magnitude may lie below the smallest subnormal value of the type of $A$ and $B$, in which case it rounds to a zero. **The sign of a null or infinite result.** The result is $-0$ or $-\infty$ when the operands have opposite signs, and $+0$ or $+\infty$ otherwise, the signs of $\pm 0$ and $\pm\infty$ being taken into account. In particular the product of two zeros is $-0$ when one of them is $-0$ and the other $+0$, and $+0$ when the two zeros have the same sign; and a nonzero exact product whose magnitude rounds to zero gives a zero of the sign of that exact product, so that an underflow may produce $-0$. **Values of the operands.** The operands may be any of the values of the type, including the special numbers $\pm 0$, $\pm\infty$ and NaN. The cases above give the result for every combination of them. Every finite value, zero and subnormal values included, is a possible operand and a possible result; the multiplication of two finite values never gives NaN. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the product of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

[E_MUL_INT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Mul** multiplies tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the product of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same signed $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \begin{cases} u & \text{if } u \le 2^{n-1}-1 \\ u - 2^n & \text{if } u \ge 2^{n-1} \end{cases} \qquad \text{where } u = \left(\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]\right) \bmod 2^n $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact product of the two elements, the product in $\mathbb{Z}$ of the two integers, before the reduction modulo $2^n$, - $x \bmod 2^n$ is the remainder of the Euclidean division of $x$ by $2^n$, taken in $[0, 2^n-1]$, i.e. the unique integer $u \in [0, 2^n-1]$ such that $x - u$ is a multiple of $2^n$, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $n$ is the number of bits of the type of $A$ and $B$. The result is thus the unique value of the type of $A$ and $B$ that is congruent to the exact product modulo $2^n$: the $2^n$ values of an $n$-bit signed type form a complete set of residues modulo $2^n$, so that exactly one of them satisfies the condition. The exact product of two values of the type lies in $\left[-2^{2n-2}+2^{n-1},\, 2^{2n-2}\right]$, and the reduction modulo $2^n$ is applied as many times as the magnitude of that product requires. **The result may differ from the exact product in magnitude and in sign.** The range of the type is not closed under multiplication, so that the product of two values of the type generally leaves it: for `int8`, $100 * 100$ gives $16$, $-100 * 100$ gives $-16$, and $100 * 3$ gives $44$. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same type and no wider type is used, so that the value of $C$ is that value of the type, sign included, and the multiplication is not monotonic on the signed integer types. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the product of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

examples.excerpt:
### Example 2

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}
  3 & 4.5 \\
  16 & 0.5 \\
  25.5 & 24
\end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = A * B = \begin{bmatrix}
  3*2 & 4.5*(-1) \\
  16*2 & 0.5*(-1) \\
  25.5*2 & 24*(-1)
\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}
  6 & -4.5 \\
  32 & -0.5 \\
  51 & -24
\end{bmatrix}
$$

Tensor $B$ has rank $1$ and tensor $A$ has rank $2$; $B$ is broadcast to the shape of $A$, so that each column of $A$ is multiplied by the corresponding element of $B$.

### Example 1

For the `int8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} -6 & 100 & -100 & 100 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 100 & 100 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 18 & 16 & -16 & 44 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The product $-6 * (-3) = 18$ lies in $[-2^7, 2^7-1]$ and is its own remainder modulo $2^8$. The product $100 * 100 = 10000$ leaves that range: its remainder modulo $2^8$ is $16$, which is at most $2^7-1=127$ and is the result. The product $-100 * 100 = -10000$ has the remainder $240$ modulo $2^8$, which is at least $2^7=128$, so the result is $240-256=-16$. The product $100 * 3 = 300$ has the remainder $44$ modulo $2^8$, which is the result. The result of the first product has the sign of the exact product, whereas the results of the other three do not.

### Example 1

For the `uint8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 200 & 35 & 16 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 100 & 5 & 16 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 18 & 32 & 175 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The products $6 * 3 = 18$ and $35 * 5 = 175$ are at most $2^8-1=255$ and are their own remainders modulo $2^8$. The product $200 * 100 = 20000$ leaves the range of the type: its remainder modulo $2^8$ is $32$, which is smaller than both operands. The product $16 * 16 = 256$ is a multiple of $2^8$ and its remainder is $0$.

entries.limitation: The third element of the example requires the smallest subnormal of the format to be known, which the profile does not expose: Sonnx.FloatFormat carries only precision and maxFinite. The rounding formalised in RoundMagNearest follows the document's literal unbounded-exponent rule, so it yields a tiny nonzero value there instead of -0; the first two elements (rounded product and overflow to +inf) are covered.

- `[E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_B_0010]` Shape compatibility - Statement: see constraint [E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_A_0010](#E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_A_0010) on tensor $A$.
- `[E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_B_0020]` Type consistency - Statement: see constraint [E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_A_0020](#E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_A_0020) on tensor $A$.

- `[E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_C_0010]` Shape definition
  - Statement: Tensor $C$ has the shape of $A$ and $B$ broadcast to a common shape.
- `[E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_C_0020]` Type consistency - Statement: see constraint [E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_A_0020](#E_MUL_INT_CONSTR_A_0020) on tensor $A$.

[E_MUL_INT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Mul** multiplies tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the product of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same signed $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \begin{cases} u & \text{if } u \le 2^{n-1}-1 \\ u - 2^n & \text{if } u \ge 2^{n-1} \end{cases} \qquad \text{where } u = \left(\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]\right) \bmod 2^n $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact product of the two elements, the product in $\mathbb{Z}$ of the two integers, before the reduction modulo $2^n$, - $x \bmod 2^n$ is the remainder of the Euclidean division of $x$ by $2^n$, taken in $[0, 2^n-1]$, i.e. the unique integer $u \in [0, 2^n-1]$ such that $x - u$ is a multiple of $2^n$, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $n$ is the number of bits of the type of $A$ and $B$. The result is thus the unique value of the type of $A$ and $B$ that is congruent to the exact product modulo $2^n$: the $2^n$ values of an $n$-bit signed type form a complete set of residues modulo $2^n$, so that exactly one of them satisfies the condition. The exact product of two values of the type lies in $\left[-2^{2n-2}+2^{n-1},\, 2^{2n-2}\right]$, and the reduction modulo $2^n$ is applied as many times as the magnitude of that product requires. **The result may differ from the exact product in magnitude and in sign.** The range of the type is not closed under multiplication, so that the product of two values of the type generally leaves it: for `int8`, $100 * 100$ gives $16$, $-100 * 100$ gives $-16$, and $100 * 3$ gives $44$. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same type and no wider type is used, so that the value of $C$ is that value of the type, sign included, and the multiplication is not monotonic on the signed integer types. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the product of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

### Example 1

For the `int8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} -6 & 100 & -100 & 100 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 100 & 100 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 18 & 16 & -16 & 44 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The product $-6 * (-3) = 18$ lies in $[-2^7, 2^7-1]$ and is its own remainder modulo $2^8$. The product $100 * 100 = 10000$ leaves that range: its remainder modulo $2^8$ is $16$, which is at most $2^7-1=127$ and is the result. The product $-100 * 100 = -10000$ has the remainder $240$ modulo $2^8$, which is at least $2^7=128$, so the result is $240-256=-16$. The product $100 * 3 = 300$ has the remainder $44$ modulo $2^8$, which is the result. The result of the first product has the sign of the exact product, whereas the results of the other three do not.

[E_MUL_UINT_FUNC_0010]
 Operator **Mul** multiplies tensor $A$ by tensor $B$ element-wise and stores the result in output tensor $C$. Each element of $C$ is the product of the elements of $A$ and $B$ that correspond to it under the broadcasting rules given below. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same unsigned $n$-bit type, and the result is a value of that type. For any [tensor index](../../common/definitions.md#tensor_index) $i$ of the result $C$: $$ C[i] = \left(\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]\right) \bmod 2^n $$ where - $\tilde{A}[i] * \tilde{B}[i]$ is the exact product of the two elements, the product in $\mathbb{Z}$ of the two integers, before the reduction modulo $2^n$, - $x \bmod 2^n$ is the remainder of the Euclidean division of $x$ by $2^n$, taken in $[0, 2^n-1]$, i.e. the unique integer $u \in [0, 2^n-1]$ such that $x - u$ is a multiple of $2^n$, - $\tilde{A}$ is tensor $A$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, and $\tilde{B}$ is tensor $B$ broadcast to the shape of $C$, - $n$ is the number of bits of the type of $A$ and $B$. The result is thus the unique value of the type of $A$ and $B$ that is congruent to the exact product modulo $2^n$: the $2^n$ values of an $n$-bit unsigned type are exactly the residues modulo $2^n$, so that the condition determines the result. The exact product of two values of the type lies in $\left[0,\, (2^n-1)^2\right]$, and the reduction modulo $2^n$ is applied as many times as the magnitude of that product requires. **The result may be smaller than both operands.** The product of two non-negative integers is at least as large as either of them when both are at least $1$, whereas the result here is reduced modulo $2^n$: for `uint8`, $200 * 100$ gives $32$, and $16 * 16$ gives $0$. Tensors $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same type and no wider type is used, so that the value of $C$ is that value of the type, and the multiplication is not monotonic on the unsigned types. **Tensors of different shapes.** Tensors $A$ and $B$ are broadcast to the shape of $C$ following the multidirectional (Numpy-style) broadcasting rules: the shapes are aligned on their last dimension; a dimension that one operand does not have, including the leading dimensions missing from the operand with the smaller rank, is treated as a dimension of size $1$; and a dimension of size $1$ is extended to the size of the corresponding dimension of the other operand. Tensor $C$ has the resulting shape. When $A$ and $B$ have the same shape, $\tilde{A}$ is $A$, $\tilde{B}$ is $B$ and $C$ has that shape. **Tensors with no dimension.** A tensor with no dimension (a rank-0 tensor) is a tensor whose shape is empty. It is broadcast to the shape of the other operand, so that each element of $C$ is the product of the two operands and $C$ has the shape of the other operand. **Zero-sized dimensions.** An operand may have a zero-sized dimension. Such a dimension is compatible with a dimension of size $1$ of the other operand, and with an equal zero-sized dimension; the corresponding dimension of $C$ then has size $0$, and $C$ is empty. [END]

### Example 1

For the `uint8` type:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 200 & 35 & 16 \end{bmatrix}
\quad
B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 100 & 5 & 16 \end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
C = \begin{bmatrix} 18 & 32 & 175 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The products $6 * 3 = 18$ and $35 * 5 = 175$ are at most $2^8-1=255$ and are their own remainders modulo $2^8$. The product $200 * 100 = 20000$ leaves the range of the type: its remainder modulo $2^8$ is $32$, which is smaller than both operands. The product $16 * 16 = 256$ is a multiple of $2^8$ and its remainder is $0$.
